3.3.2. 
Pre-In-Service Termination Costs and Construction Security. If the Large 
Load Facility, its associated request for service, or any associated Large Load-
Driven Upgrade is cancelled, abandoned, or otherwise terminated before an 
applicable Large Load-Driven Upgrade reaches its Upgrade In-Service Date, 
Eligible Customer shall be responsible for all actual and reasonable costs 
prudently incurred or irrevocably committed by DesertLink with respect to that 
Large Load-Driven Upgrade that have not otherwise been recovered by 
DesertLink (“Pre-In-Service Termination Costs”). Pre-In-Service Termination 
Costs include costs incurred before or after the applicable cancellation,

11 
 
abandonment, or termination to wind down, secure, remove, or otherwise address 
the unfinished Large Load-Driven Upgrade. 
Pre-In-Service Termination Costs include, as applicable: 
(a) engineering, design, study, permitting, environmental, siting, land and land-
right, procurement, construction, testing, project management, legal, 
regulatory, and administrative costs; 
(b) vendor and contractor cancellation charges, termination charges, change-
order costs, restocking charges, demobilization costs, contract closeout costs, 
and third-party claims; 
(c) the costs of securing, preserving, mothballing, relocating, redeploying, 
dismantling, removing, transporting, storing, selling, or disposing of 
equipment, materials, and partially completed facilities; 
(d) site restoration, environmental remediation, and the restoration or 
modification of DesertLink’s existing facilities made necessary by the 
cancellation or abandonment; 
(e) Allowance for Funds Used During Construction (“AFUDC”) properly 
accrued in accordance with the Commission’s Uniform System of Accounts 
through the date on which the applicable construction activities cease or the 
applicable project is determined to have been abandoned, excluding AFUDC 
associated with amounts of Construction Work in Progress included in rate 
base or otherwise recovered through rates; and 
(f) any other costs reasonably incurred by DesertLink as a direct result of the 
cancellation, abandonment, suspension, or termination. 
DesertLink may draw upon and apply Construction Security to Pre-In-Service 
Termination Costs as such costs are incurred or the associated obligations 
become fixed and payable. DesertLink may retain Construction Security until all 
Pre-In-Service Termination Costs are reasonably determinable and DesertLink 
has served on Eligible Customer a final statement reconciling Pre-In-Service 
Termination Costs, Construction Security applied, and the recoveries described 
in this Section, together with supporting information (the “Termination Cost 
Reconciliation”). Construction Security does not limit Eligible Customer’s 
underlying liability. Eligible Customer shall pay any deficiency within ten (10) 
Business Days after receipt of the Termination Cost Reconciliation. The 
Termination Cost Reconciliation shall become final in the same manner and 
within the same period as a Reconciliation Statement under Section 6.6, and 
DesertLink shall release any excess Construction Security after the Termination 
Cost Reconciliation becomes final, including through resolution of any dispute 
under Article 11. Construction Security applied under this Section does not 
constitute Applied Security Proceeds and does not produce a TRBAA Credit 
except to the extent provided in Section 3.3.3(d). Nothing in this Agreement 
limits DesertLink’s right to seek recovery of unpaid Pre-In-Service Termination 
Costs through its Formula Rate or otherwise as the Commission may authorize.

Termination Costs, provided that DesertLink shall not be required to take any 
action inconsistent with prudent utility practice, safety requirements, Applicable 
Laws and Regulations, existing contractual obligations, or the reliable operation 
of its transmission facilities. The Termination Cost Reconciliation shall reflect, 
when realized, applicable vendor refunds, insurance recoveries, net salvage 
proceeds, reuse or redeployment credits, and other recoveries attributable to the 
cancelled or abandoned scope, but shall not credit amounts representing 
DesertLink’s lawfully earned return or carrying costs except to the extent 
necessary to prevent duplicate recovery. 
This Section applies separately to each Large Load-Driven Upgrade. If one or 
more Large Load-Driven Upgrades have reached their Upgrade In-Service Dates 
when the Large Load Facility or associated request for service is cancelled, this 
Section shall apply only to the Large Load-Driven Upgrades and portions of the 
project that have not reached their Upgrade In-Service Dates. The treatment of 
each Large Load-Driven Upgrade that has reached its Upgrade In-Service Date 
shall be governed by Section 3.3.4 and Articles 6 and 7. 
3.3.3. 
Rate Base and Formula Rate Treatment Before an Upgrade In-Service 
Date. To the extent costs associated with a cancelled or abandoned Large Load-
Driven Upgrade that has not reached its Upgrade In-Service Date have been 
included in Construction Work in Progress or any other component of 
DesertLink’s rate base, DesertLink shall, consistent with the Commission’s 
Uniform System of Accounts, its Formula Rate and Protocols, and other

(a) remove, reclassify, or otherwise exclude such costs from rate base to the

requirements; 
(b) reflect that treatment in the next practicable Annual Update and 
corresponding true-up; 
(c) cease accruing AFUDC to the extent and at the time required by the

(d) make any adjustment or credit necessary to prevent DesertLink from

Rate. 
Any depreciation, amortization, or other amount recovered through DesertLink’s

Application of Construction Security shall not require DesertLink to refund or

surrender any return, carrying cost, tax allowance, or other amount lawfully

(b) require the removal from rate base of a Large Load-Driven Upgrade or a

Responsibility; or 
(d) terminate, reduce, or excuse Eligible Customer’s obligation to pay the 
Supplemental MTRC and prior-period true-up adjustments under Section 6.6,

Cumulative Revenue Responsibility. 
Upon any effective termination of this Agreement, or upon the permanent

6. Cost Recovery  
6.1. 
Cost Recovery and Minimum Contribution. DesertLink shall include the Large

does not remove any Covered Upgrade from rate base or require a capital-cost

19 
 
MTRC only to the extent forecast or actual Qualifying Transmission Revenues are less 
than the applicable Annual MTRC. The Annual MTRC is a revenue floor, not an 
additive charge, and does not alter CAISO cost allocation or DesertLink plant

Eligible Customer acknowledges that DesertLink will incur costs and undertake 
planning, engineering, procurement, and construction in reliance on the Large Load 
Facility’s development and operation. Eligible Customer therefore accepts the

6.2. 
Qualifying Transmission Revenues. For each Rate Year or partial Rate Year, 
“Qualifying Transmission Revenues” means wholesale transmission revenues paid by 
or on behalf of Eligible Customer under the CAISO Tariff or another Commission-
accepted arrangement that are attributable to service to the Large Load Facility and 
reduce transmission revenues otherwise collected from CAISO customers or directly 
credit DesertLink’s Net Revenue Requirement. Qualifying Transmission Revenues 
include: (a) the portion of TAC revenue attributable to the Large Load Facility and 
allocable to DesertLink under the reproducible methodology in Schedule 2; and (b) 
Wheeling Access Charges and other wholesale transmission-access, wheeling, or 
transmission-service charges paid to CAISO, a Participating TO, or a non-PTO 
transmission or load-serving entity for deliveries serving the Large Load Facility, but 
only to the extent they reduce transmission revenues otherwise collected through TAC 
or directly credit DesertLink’s Net Revenue Requirement and are not otherwise 
reflected as a credit in calculating the Annual MTRC, the Supplemental MTRC, or a 
TRBAA Credit. Qualifying Transmission Revenues do not include Supplemental 
MTRC Receipts, Applied Security Proceeds, retail charges, or amounts that do not 
reduce transmission revenues otherwise collected from CAISO customers or directly 
credit DesertLink’s Net Revenue Requirement. 
6.3. 
Annual MTRC and Allocation.  
6.3.1. Upgrade-Specific MTRC Calculation. DesertLink shall calculate a separate 
Annual MTRC for each Covered Upgrade solely under the MTRC Calculation 
Template in Schedule 5. Before the Final MTRC Determination Date, DesertLink 
shall calculate and update the Estimated Annual MTRC from the then-current 
estimated capital cost. Within one (1) year after the applicable Covered Upgrade 
enters service, when the actual capital cost of that Covered Upgrade is known and 
all costs associated with its estimated capital cost have been accounted for,

20 
 
DesertLink shall establish the Final Annual MTRC using final incurred capital cost 
and the Project-Specific Levelized Fixed Charge Rate calculated under Schedule 5. 
Schedule 5 shall calculate the Project-Specific Levelized Fixed Charge Rate by: (i) 
determining the present-worth revenue requirement using the applicable capital 
structure, cost of debt, return on equity, federal and state income-tax rates, income-
tax conversion factor, and levelized-depreciation schedule; (ii) applying a 
depreciation rate of five percent (5%) of the applicable capital cost input in each 
year of the twenty (20)-year MTRC Term to calculate present-worth federal and 
state income-tax depreciation benefits; (iii) annualizing the resulting present-worth 
revenue requirement over the MTRC Term using the applicable after-tax discount 
rate and annualization factor; and (iv) adding the fixed expense allocator specified 
in Schedule 5. The Final Annual MTRC shall equal the applicable final incurred 
capital cost multiplied by the resulting Project-Specific Levelized Fixed Charge 
Rate. No component reflected in the Project-Specific Levelized Fixed Charge Rate 
or the fixed expense allocator shall be added again as a separate component of the 
Annual MTRC. The Final Annual MTRC and the Schedule 5 inputs used to 
calculate it are fixed as of the Final MTRC Determination Date and shall not be 
recalculated for later changes in actual cost, Formula Rate inputs, or other cost-of-
service components, except to correct an error or fraud, to implement an effective 
prospective reassignment, to implement a final FERC order applicable to the 
calculation, or to reflect, prospectively, a change in (i) DesertLink’s return on equity 
component of its Formula Rate, resulting from a final FERC order accepting or 
approving such change, or (ii) applicable federal or state income tax rates or income 
tax law enacted after the Final MTRC Determination Date; provided that, the five 
percent (5%) annual levelized-depreciation schedule in Schedule 5 shall remain 
fixed for the MTRC Term unless a final FERC order requires otherwise. If 
DesertLink adjusts the Final Annual MTRC after the Final MTRC Determination 
Date pursuant to the foregoing provision, DesertLink shall update the MTRC 
Calculation Template and serve it upon Eligible Customer in accordance with the 
notice provisions contained in this Agreement. Upon such service to Eligible 
Customer, the updated MTRC Calculation Template shall replace the existing 
MTRC Calculation Template in its entirety and become effective on the date of such 
service. The foregoing effectiveness of an updated MTRC Calculation Template 
does not preclude Eligible Customer from disputing any change to the MTRC 
Calculation Template pursuant to Article 11 of this Agreement. Any resulting 
adjustment to the Total Required Revenue Commitment shall apply only to the Rate 
Years remaining in the MTRC Term as provided in Section 6.7. 
Each Annual MTRC shall apply for its separate twenty (20)-year MTRC Term, with 
the initial and final partial Rate Years prorated based on the number of monthly 
Billing Periods in the applicable Rate Year during which the Covered Upgrade is in 
service. Schedule 1 shall identify the initial Estimated Annual MTRC and initial 
projected Total Required Revenue Commitment for each Large Load-Driven 
Upgrade, and Schedule 5 shall record the Final MTRC Determination Date, Final 
Annual MTRC, Total Required Revenue Commitment, and the completed 
calculation for each Covered Upgrade. Schedule 4 shall provide the corresponding

21 
 
project-specific information for a DesertLink-owned CAISO-Assigned Regional 
Project, if applicable. 
6.3.2. Initial Allocation. Schedule 1 shall identify, separately for each Large Load-

(d) any portion of the facility determined at the outset to serve other

6.4. 
Supplemental MTRC. Beginning on the in-service date of each Covered Upgrade,

charges shall be reconciled in the next Reconciliation Statement under Section 6.6.

specific Covered Upgrade shall be applied to that upgrade. Qualifying Transmission 
Revenues not attributable to a specific Covered Upgrade shall be allocated among the

prorated Annual MTRCs for the applicable period. 
The calculation may be expressed as: 
Supplemental MTRC = max (applicable Annual MTRC − Qualifying Transmission 
Revenues, $0). 
The Annual MTRC is not an annual true-up of project cost or Formula Rate inputs.

24 
 
proration, effective prospective reassignment, and correction of error, fraud, a final

MTRC from Schedule 5. DesertLink shall identify, by Eligible Customer and Covered

Proceeds applied to identified obligations, direct recoveries, closing unpaid billed 
balance, and each Annual Termination Fee Credit. Concurrently with each Annual

An unpaid Supplemental MTRC remains due from Eligible Customer and, when later 
received or satisfied through Applied Security Proceeds, is recorded in the TRBA only 
in the Rate Year of receipt or application. The Reconciliation Statement shall not 
reopen the Final Annual MTRC or Total Required Revenue Commitment except as 
expressly allowed by Section 6.3.1. 
The difference between the Supplemental MTRC billed for a Rate Year, excluding any 
prior-period true-up adjustment included in that billing, and the actual Supplemental

25 
 
MTRC determined in the Reconciliation Statement for that Rate Year shall constitute a 
“prior-period true-up adjustment,” which shall increase (if under-billed) or reduce (if 
over-billed) the projected Supplemental MTRC invoiced under Section 6.5 following 
the next Annual Projection. If no further Supplemental MTRC will be invoiced under 
this Agreement, DesertLink shall invoice any under-billed amount, payable within 
thirty (30) Calendar Days after receipt of the invoice, and shall refund any over-billed 
amount to Eligible Customer within thirty (30) Calendar Days after service of the 
Reconciliation Statement. No interest shall accrue on the Supplemental MTRC or on 
any prior-period true-up adjustment, invoice, refund, or other adjustment of the 
Supplemental MTRC between DesertLink and Eligible Customer. Any refund to 
Eligible Customer of an amount previously recorded as a TRBAA Credit shall be 
reversed in the TRBA when paid, and any under-billed amount later received shall be 
recorded in the TRBA when received, in each case as provided in Section 6.8. Any 
amount returned by DesertLink to transmission customers through the TRBAA shall 
include interest as provided in Section 5.5 of the TO Tariff. 
A Reconciliation Statement shall become final on the earlier of (a) Eligible 
Customer’s written acceptance of the Reconciliation Statement or (b) ninety (90) 
Calendar Days after service, unless before that date Eligible Customer serves a Notice 
of Dispute under Section 11.1 identifying with reasonable specificity the items 
disputed. If a Notice of Dispute is timely served, the undisputed portions of the 
Reconciliation Statement shall become final on the date that would otherwise apply, 
and the disputed items shall become final upon the applicable Dispute Determination 
under Section 11.5. A final Reconciliation Statement may be revised only to 
implement a Dispute Determination, to reflect CAISO resettlements or other corrected 
data as provided in Schedule 2, or to correct errors or fraud. Finality of a 
Reconciliation Statement under this Agreement does not affect the Commission’s 
review and approval of any TRBAA. 
For purposes of this Agreement, Supplemental MTRC Receipts exclude Applied 
Security Proceeds. Applied Security Proceeds shall be counted only when DesertLink 
applies such proceeds to satisfy an identified payment obligation and shall reduce that 
obligation dollar-for-dollar. The posting, maintenance, replenishment, drawing, or 
holding of Security shall not, by itself, constitute a Supplemental MTRC Receipt, an 
Applied Security Proceed, satisfaction of the Cumulative Revenue Responsibility, or a 
TRBAA Credit. 
No amount shall be counted both as a Supplemental MTRC Receipt and as an Applied 
Security Proceed. If DesertLink receives payment of an obligation previously satisfied 
through Applied Security Proceeds, DesertLink shall not count the subsequent 
payment toward the Cumulative Revenue Responsibility or a TRBAA Credit and shall 
instead return the duplicative amount, release an equivalent amount of Security, or, 
with supporting notice to Eligible Customer, apply the amount to another then-
outstanding obligation under this Agreement. 
6.7. 
Cumulative Revenue Responsibility and Break-Even. DesertLink shall maintain a 
Cumulative Revenue Ledger for each Covered Upgrade and shall update it at least

26 
 
annually in connection with the Annual Update. DesertLink shall include an updated 
Cumulative Revenue Ledger statement, with supporting workpapers, in each 
Reconciliation Statement served on Eligible Customer under Section 6.6. For each 
Covered Upgrade, the Total Required Revenue Commitment equals the Final Annual 
MTRC multiplied by twenty (20), adjusted only for partial-year proration and any 
prospective recalculation of the Final Annual MTRC permitted by Section 6.3.1, 
which shall apply only to the Rate Years remaining in the MTRC Term after the 
recalculation takes effect. Until the Final MTRC Determination Date, the projected 
Total Required Revenue Commitment shall equal the Estimated Annual MTRC 
multiplied by twenty (20). 
Remaining Cumulative Revenue Responsibility equals the applicable Total Required 
Revenue Commitment less: 
(a) cumulative Qualifying Transmission Revenues; 
(b) cumulative Supplemental MTRC Receipts; 
(c) cumulative Applied Security Proceeds; 
(d) effective prospective reassignment credits; and 
(e) cash amounts received and applied toward the Termination Fee, excluding any 
portion satisfied through Applied Security Proceeds already counted under 
clause (c). 
Each dollar shall be entered in the Cumulative Revenue Ledger only once. 
Supplemental MTRC Receipts shall exclude Applied Security Proceeds. Applied 
Security Proceeds shall be entered only when applied to an identified Supplemental 
MTRC, prior-period true-up adjustment, Termination Fee, or other payment obligation 
under Article 6 or Section 3.3.4. Security that is posted, drawn but not applied, held as

Termination Fee Balance shall be separately identified in the Reconciliation Statement 
and in the workpapers required under Section 6.8 and shall not again reduce the 
Cumulative Revenue Responsibility. 
If an amount previously credited in the Cumulative Revenue Ledger is subsequently 
refunded, reversed, disallowed, or otherwise ceases to satisfy the applicable obligation, 
DesertLink shall make a corresponding adjustment to the ledger, subject to the finality 
and no-revival provisions of this Section. 
Cancellation, downsizing, curtailment, or departure does not extinguish the remaining 
responsibility. When a final Reconciliation Statement determines that the 
responsibility has reached zero (“Break-Even”), DesertLink shall terminate the 
operational payment and Security obligations and release any excess Security. Once 
finally satisfied, the responsibility shall not revive because of a later change in ROE, 
expense, load, forecast, or other Formula Rate input, subject only to final true-ups and 
correction of errors or fraud for periods before satisfaction.

6.8. 
TRBAA Credit and No Double Recovery. Supplemental MTRC Receipts, Applied 
Security Proceeds other than Applied Security Proceeds applied to a Termination Fee, 
Annual Termination Fee Credits, and any duplicate-recovery credit under Section 
3.3.3(d) or Section 6.3.5 shall be credited to transmission customers solely through the 
TRBAA and shall not be recorded as revenue credits in, or otherwise included as

Section 6.5; and (b) for any Covered Upgrade with a Termination Fee Balance, the 
Annual Termination Fee Credit scheduled under Section 3.3.4 for the following Rate 
Year, prorated as applicable and limited to the available Termination Fee Balance. 
DesertLink shall record in the TRBA only Supplemental MTRC cash receipts, Applied 
Security Proceeds other than Applied Security Proceeds applied to a Termination Fee, 
and Annual Termination Fee Credits actually received, applied, or scheduled for the 
applicable Rate Year, respectively. Applied Security Proceeds applied to a 
Termination Fee shall be deposited into and held in the Termination Fee Account 
under Section 3.3.4 and shall be credited to transmission customers solely through the 
applicable Annual Termination Fee Credits. The difference between the Forecast 
TRBAA Credit and those actual amounts shall be reflected in the principal balance of 
the TRBA and flowed through to transmission customers in a subsequent TRBAA. A 
billed but unpaid Supplemental MTRC is not a TRBAA Credit. A later Supplemental 
MTRC Receipt or Applied Security Proceeds, other than Applied Security Proceeds 
applied to a Termination Fee, shall be recorded only in the Rate Year in which it is 
received or applied, respectively. Any amount previously recorded as a TRBAA Credit 
that is later refunded, reversed, or otherwise ceases to satisfy the applicable obligation 
shall be reversed in the TRBA when refunded or reversed. Interest on the TRBA 
balance shall be calculated as provided in Section 5.5 of the TO Tariff. Qualifying 
Transmission Revenues shall not be included again as a TRBAA Credit because they 
are already reflected in calculating the Supplemental MTRC. 
Each dollar shall be included in a TRBAA Credit only once. Applied Security 
Proceeds shall not also be treated as Supplemental MTRC Receipts, and the posting, 
drawing, holding, replenishment, replacement, or return of Security shall not 
independently produce a TRBAA Credit. A Forecast TRBAA Credit applies only to 
the forecast Rate Year and shall be reconciled through the TRBA to actual 
Supplemental MTRC Receipts, Applied Security Proceeds other than those applied to 
a Termination Fee, and Annual Termination Fee Credits, as applicable. 
DesertLink shall maintain workpapers reconciling each Forecast TRBAA Credit and 
each amount recorded in the TRBA under this Section 6.8 to the applicable Annual 
MTRC calculation in Schedule 5, forecast and actual Qualifying Transmission 
Revenues, opening unpaid billed balance, Supplemental MTRC invoiced, prior-period 
true-up adjustment, Supplemental MTRC cash receipt, Applied Security Proceed, 
direct recovery, closing unpaid billed balance, Termination Fee Balance, Annual 
Termination Fee Credit, resulting forecast-to-actual TRBA difference, Rate Year, 
Large Load Customer, and Covered Upgrade. DesertLink shall include with each

28 
 
TRBAA filing workpapers sufficient to permit transmission customers to verify the 
TRBAA Credits reflected in that TRBAA, which may present customer-specific 
information on an aggregated basis or be submitted subject to a request for privileged 
treatment under 18 C.F.R. § 388.112 or other appropriate confidentiality protections. 
6.9. 
Prospective Reassignment of Revenue Responsibility.  
6.9.1. Eligibility for Reassignment of Revenue Responsibility. Whether or not the 
Large Load Customer remains in service, a portion of the prospective revenue 
responsibility associated with a Large Load-Driven Upgrade may be reassigned to a 
subsequent load customer if an objective transmission study conducted under the 
applicable tariff or study process determines that: 
(a) the subsequent large load customer relies upon identifiable incremental 
capability created by the Large Load-Driven Upgrade; and 
(b) that reliance avoids or reduces identifiable transmission upgrades that 
otherwise would have been required to provide the subsequent large load 
customer’s requested service. 
Incidental power flows, generalized system benefits, or use of the transmission 
system that does not satisfy both requirements shall not support a reassignment. 
This Section 6.9 applies only to a load customer other than the Large Load 
Customer, at a facility other than the Large Load Facility. It does not apply to a 
transfer of ownership or operation of the Large Load Facility, a change in Eligible 
Customer, or an assignment of this Agreement, which are governed by Sections 
6.10 and 10.1 and do not alter the Applicable Allocation Percentage or the Large 
Load-Driven Upgrades attributable to the Large Load Facility. 
6.9.2. Reassignment Calculation. DesertLink shall determine the prospective 
reassignment separately for each Large Load-Driven Upgrade satisfying Section 
6.9.1 (each, a “Shared Upgrade”). For each Shared Upgrade: 
(a) the Demonstrated Avoided Upgrade Cost shall equal the reasonable 
estimated cost of the transmission upgrades that would have been required 
for the subsequent large load customer absent the Shared Upgrade, less the 
reasonable estimated cost of any additional transmission upgrades required 
when the capability of the Shared Upgrade is considered; 
(b) the Remaining Allocated Net Plant shall equal the portion of the Shared 
Upgrade’s net plant balance included in rate base immediately before the 
reassignment that remains assigned to the Large Load Customer under this 
Agreement; 
(c) the Capability-Supported Amount shall equal the portion of the Remaining 
Allocated Net Plant reasonably attributable to the incremental capability of 
the Shared Upgrade actually relied upon by the subsequent large load 
customer; and 
(d) the Reassigned Investment Amount shall equal the least of:

29 
 
(i) the Demonstrated Avoided Upgrade Cost; 
(ii) the Capability-Supported Amount; and 
(iii) the Remaining Allocated Net Plant. 
The Demonstrated Avoided Upgrade Cost, Capability-Supported Amount, and 
Remaining Allocated Net Plant shall be determined using a consistent cost basis and 
price year. If Remaining Allocated Net Plant is greater than zero, the Reassignment 
Percentage shall equal the Reassigned Investment Amount divided by the 
Remaining Allocated Net Plant, bounded between zero and one hundred percent 
(100%). If Remaining Allocated Net Plant is zero or negative, no Reassignment 
Percentage shall be calculated under this methodology; any reassignment shall 
require an applicable tariff methodology or Commission determination addressing 
that circumstance. 
6.9.3. Prospective Adjustment of Revenue Responsibility. Beginning on the 
Reassignment Effective Date, the applicable Annual MTRC assigned to the Large 
Load Customer shall be prospectively reduced by the Reassignment Percentage 
applied to the Shared Upgrade. DesertLink shall record a separate effective 
prospective reassignment credit in the Cumulative Revenue Ledger equal to the 
Reassignment Percentage multiplied by the Remaining Cumulative Revenue 
Responsibility associated with the Shared Upgrade that remains assigned to the 
Large Load Customer immediately before the Reassignment Effective Date. That 
credit shall be the sole Cumulative Revenue Ledger adjustment for the reassigned 
responsibility. It shall not adjust the Total Required Revenue Commitment or result 
in a second reduction to the Remaining Cumulative Revenue Responsibility or 
Required Operational Security for the same reassigned responsibility. 
DesertLink shall recalculate the Supplemental MTRC and Operational Security 
under this Agreement to reflect the reassignment. The Reassignment Effective Date 
shall be the latest of: 
(a) the date the subsequent large load customer commences the service for 
which the Shared Upgrade provides the identified incremental capability; 
(b) the effective date of a cost recovery agreement establishing the subsequent 
large load customer’s corresponding revenue responsibility; 
(c) the date on which all Security required from the eligible customer serving 
the subsequent large load customer becomes effective; and 
(d) the date on which the study and any other approvals required under the 
applicable tariff become final. 
No reduction in the Large Load Customer’s Operational Security shall occur until 
the corresponding responsibility and required Security have become effective for the 
subsequent large load customer. 
6.9.4. Prospective Treatment and Prevention of Duplicate Reassignment. A 
reassignment under this Section shall:

30 
 
(a) operate prospectively only and shall not produce a refund, credit, or 
reopening of amounts properly determined for a prior Rate Year; 
(b) transfer prospective revenue responsibility only and shall not constitute a 
sale or transfer of transmission facilities, a transfer of plant ownership, a 
change in plant accounting, or a modification of any CAISO cost allocation; 
(c) not exceed the prospective responsibility remaining under this Agreement 
for the Shared Upgrade; and 
(d) not assign the same transmission capability, avoided upgrade cost, Annual 
MTRC, or Cumulative Revenue Responsibility to more than one large load 
customer. 
DesertLink shall maintain an upgrade-specific reassignment ledger identifying the 
capability and responsibility assigned to each large load customer. Once 
responsibility has been effectively reassigned, that responsibility shall not revert to 
the Large Load Customer if the subsequent large load customer later terminates, 
reduces, or fails to commence service. The reassigned responsibility shall instead 
remain with the subsequent large load customer and the Eligible Customer 
responsible for its payment, subject to any further prospective reassignment 
permitted under the applicable agreement and tariff. 
Any prospective reassignment, adjustment, or change in the cost share of a CAISO-
Assigned Regional Project shall be recognized under this Agreement only to the 
extent authorized or required by the CAISO Tariff or a Commission-accepted 
methodology. DesertLink shall apply an effective change prospectively to the 
Regional Project Allocated ARR, Cumulative Revenue Responsibility, 
Supplemental MTRC, TRBAA Credit, and Operational Security, and shall update 
Schedule 4 and the applicable workpapers. The change shall not assign the same 
project share to more than one customer or alter costs allocated to other customers 
under the CAISO Tariff. 
6.10. Change in Eligible Customer. Cost responsibility is assigned to the Large Load 
Customer and Large Load Facility, as paid by the Eligible Customer then taking 
wholesale transmission service on behalf of the Large Load Customer and Large Load 
Facility. If the Eligible Customer serving a Large Load Customer or Large Load 
Facility changes, the Successor Eligible Customer must execute an assumption 
agreement covering the Cumulative Revenue Responsibility and any outstanding 
obligations under Section 6.3.6, provide required Security, and become responsible on 
a date coordinated with CAISO billing before the prior Eligible Customer is released. 
Following the complete departure of the Large Load Customer, the last responsible 
Eligible Customer remains obligated unless responsibility is transferred under an 
applicable tariff or state-law mechanism, assumed by a successor, or prospectively 
reassigned as permitted under this Agreement and the CAISO Requirements. If 
ownership or operation of the Large Load Facility is transferred, Eligible Customer 
shall notify DesertLink within thirty (30) Calendar Days and shall cause the transferee 
to execute a Limited Acknowledgment in the form attached to this Agreement. The 
transfer shall not alter the Applicable Allocation Percentage, Cumulative Revenue 
Responsibility, or Security obligations under this Agreement.

31 
 
A sale, lease, or other transfer of the Large Load Facility, or of the Large Load 
Customer’s interest in such Large Load Facility, is not a reassignment under Section 
6.9 and does not require a study under Section 6.9.1. Cost responsibility shall continue 
to follow the Large Load Facility, the transferee shall execute a Limited 
Acknowledgment substantially in the form included in this Agreement, and Eligible

6.11. CAISO Data and Settlement Coordination. Eligible Customer shall provide 
DesertLink, or authorize and direct its Scheduling Coordinator, Utility Distribution

To the extent authorized or required by the CAISO Tariff, CAISO may provide or

imposes an obligation on CAISO or makes CAISO a party to this Agreement. 
DesertLink and Eligible Customer shall cooperate with CAISO and other applicable

exchanges, and authorizations identified in Schedule 2. 
DesertLink shall calculate Qualifying Transmission Revenues, the Annual MTRC, and

If final data are not available when a calculation is required, DesertLink may use

6.12. Information Rights and Confidentiality. Upon reasonable request, DesertLink shall 
provide Eligible Customer the workpapers, data, and other information reasonably

16.3 of the TO Tariff, the CAISO Tariff, and any applicable confidentiality agreement.

7. Security and Payment Obligations 
7.1. 
Construction Security. Before an applicable Large Load-Driven Upgrade reaches its 
Upgrade In-Service Date, Eligible Customer shall maintain Construction Security 
under the relevant agreement sufficient to secure: 
(a) DesertLink’s incurred and irrevocably committed engineering, design, 
procurement, permitting, construction, testing, and related costs attributable 
to that upgrade; and 
(b) the Pre-In-Service Termination Costs described in Section 3.3.2, including 
properly accrued AFUDC and applicable cancellation, demobilization, 
equipment removal, disposition, remediation, and restoration costs 
(“Construction Security”).  
Construction Security secures, but does not limit, Eligible Customer’s liability for 
those amounts. Construction Security provided under the relevant Interconnection 
Agreement or an engineering and procurement agreement for the same costs shall 
count toward, and shall not be duplicated by, the Construction Security required under 
this Agreement. Construction Security shall remain in effect for each Large Load-
Driven Upgrade until that upgrade reaches its Upgrade In-Service Date and the 
applicable release or conversion conditions in Section 7.2 are satisfied. 
A Large Load-Driven Upgrade reaching its Upgrade In-Service Date shall not result in 
the release of Construction Security attributable to another Large Load-Driven 
Upgrade that has not reached its Upgrade In-Service Date. Eligible Customer shall 
replenish Construction Security within ten (10) Business Days after notice of a 
permitted draw and supporting information if additional secured obligations remain 
and the remaining Construction Security is less than the amount required under this 
Section. 
For a CAISO-Assigned Regional Project owned by DesertLink, any pre-service 
payment, contribution, or security required from Eligible Customer for its formally 
assigned share shall be provided only as required by the CAISO Tariff, an applicable 
Interconnection Agreement, or another Commission-accepted arrangement, and shall 
be identified in Schedule 4. This Agreement does not independently require pre-
service Construction Security solely because CAISO has assigned a share of a regional 
project to the Large Load Facility. The treatment of costs for a cancelled or abandoned 
regional project shall be governed by Section 6.3.5 and the applicable Commission 
order, CAISO Tariff, and any project-specific abandoned-plant incentive authorized by 
the Commission. For a project owned by another entity, construction and operational 
security shall be provided under the CAISO Tariff or the arrangement required by 
Section 6.3.6 and Schedule 4; it shall not be treated as DesertLink Operational 
Security unless included in DesertLink’s Formula Rate and expressly identified as 
DesertLink’s share. 
7.2. 
Delivery of Operational Security. No later than thirty (30) Calendar Days before the 
earliest expected Upgrade In-Service Date identified in Schedule 1 or Regional Project

33 
 
In-Service Date identified in Schedule 4 for a DesertLink-owned CAISO-Assigned 
Regional Project, Eligible Customer shall deliver Operational Security calculated 
under this Article for the Large Load-Driven Upgrades and DesertLink-owned 
CAISO-Assigned Regional Project expected to enter service. Operational Security 
must be fully effective before any applicable Upgrade In-Service Date or Regional 
Project In-Service Date.  
If different Large Load-Driven Upgrades or DesertLink-owned CAISO-Assigned 
Regional Projects are expected to reach their applicable in-service dates on different 
dates, DesertLink shall recalculate the Required Operational Security before each 
subsequent in-service date to include the additional Cumulative Revenue 
Responsibility attributable to the upgrade or project share entering service. Eligible 
Customer shall provide any resulting increase no later than fifteen (15) Business Days 
after receipt of a Security Notice, or by the applicable in-service date if earlier. 
Inclusion of pre-service Construction Work in Progress in rate base shall not constitute 
an Upgrade In-Service Date or independently trigger the Operational Security 
requirement. Construction Security shall remain applicable to each Large Load-Driven 
Upgrade that has not reached its Upgrade In-Service Date. 
No Construction Security attributable to a Large Load-Driven Upgrade shall be 
released or converted unless:  
(a) the Required Operational Security attributable to that upgrade is effective; 
(b) that upgrade has reached its Upgrade In-Service Date; and 
(c) DesertLink has determined that all Pre-In-Service Termination Costs and 
other construction-related obligations attributable to that upgrade have been 
paid or adequately reserved for. 
Any portion of Construction Security retained for unresolved construction costs shall 
be released after DesertLink determines that those costs have been paid or adequately 
reserved for or, if Section 3.3.2 applies, after the Termination Cost Reconciliation 
becomes final. Failure to timely deliver Required Operational Security is a default 
permitting DesertLink, to the extent authorized by the applicable tariffs and 
agreements, to suspend energization or service, terminate applicable interconnection 
arrangements, and draw Construction Security for secured obligations.  
7.3. 
Required Operational Security. Required Operational Security shall equal one 
hundred percent (100%) of the nominal Remaining Cumulative Revenue 
Responsibility. DesertLink shall reduce that amount only by the portion of Qualifying 
Retail Security Support identified in a currently effective Retail Security Certification. 
A Retail Security Certification is accepted in reliance on Eligible Customer’s 
representations and does not require DesertLink to review the underlying retail-
security documents in the ordinary course. If DesertLink has a reasonable basis to 
question the certification, or after a payment default, Credit Review Event, or Material 
Adverse Credit Event, DesertLink may request supporting information reasonably 
necessary to verify continued compliance. Any resulting deficiency shall be delivered

34 
 
or restored within fifteen (15) Business Days after receipt of a Security Notice, or by 
the applicable in-service date if earlier. 
7.4. 
Annual Resizing and Security Notices. DesertLink shall recalculate Required 
Operational Security with each Annual Projection, Final MTRC Determination Date, 
recalculation of a Final Annual MTRC under Section 6.3.1, Reconciliation Statement, 
effective prospective reassignment, replacement or expiration of Qualifying Retail 
Security Support, or Credit Review Event. If DesertLink reasonably determines that 
the Required Security Amount exceeds available Security, it may issue a Security 
Notice identifying the required increase or restoration and reasonable supporting detail 
then available. Eligible Customer shall provide the required increase or restoration 
within fifteen (15) Business Days after receipt of the Security Notice, or by the 
applicable in-service date if earlier. A reduction shall be released only after the 
relevant calculation and reconciliation are final. 
7.5. 
Form of Operational Security. Except to the extent of currently effective Qualifying 
Retail Security Support, Eligible Customer shall provide direct Operational Security in 
the form of cash, an irrevocable standby Letter of Credit meeting Schedule 3, or any 
combination of cash and Letter of Credit. DesertLink may accept another form of 
Security that it determines, in its sole discretion, is acceptable. 
Each Letter of Credit shall have an initial stated term of at least twelve (12) months 
and shall remain continuously effective until released under this Agreement; provided, 
however, that a Letter of Credit may have a stated expiration date before its release 
date if Eligible Customer timely extends or replaces it so that Security in an amount 
not less than the Required Security Amount remains continuously available to 
DesertLink.  
If an issuing bank has the right not to renew a Letter of Credit, the Letter of Credit 
shall require the issuing bank to provide DesertLink and Eligible Customer at least 
ninety (90) Calendar Days’ prior written notice of nonrenewal. Eligible Customer shall 
provide a conforming extension or replacement Letter of Credit, or additional cash 
collateral or other Security accepted by DesertLink, no later than sixty (60) Calendar 
Days before the applicable expiration date.   
If Eligible Customer fails to provide the required extension, replacement, or other 
Security by that deadline, DesertLink may, before the Letter of Credit expires, draw all 
or any portion of the then-available amount under the Letter of Credit and retain the 
proceeds as cash collateral, apply the proceeds to secured obligations, or both. Any 
proceeds retained but not applied shall continue to constitute Security until released 
under this Agreement. 
7.6. 
Draw and Application. DesertLink may draw against all or any portion of a Letter of 
Credit, apply cash collateral, or apply another form of Security accepted by 
DesertLink to secured obligations upon: (a) an unpaid Supplemental MTRC, true-up, 
Termination Fee, or other amount due after the applicable payment period; (b) Eligible 
Customer’s failure to timely deliver, maintain, replace, restore, or increase Security;

35 
 
(c) cancellation, termination, withdrawal, abandonment, or permanent cessation of the 
Large Load Facility or a material breach of this Agreement; (d) a material inaccuracy 
in a Retail Security Certification or Security instrument; (e) Eligible Customer: (i) files 
a voluntary petition in bankruptcy or seeks reorganization, arrangement, or similar 
relief under any bankruptcy, insolvency, or debtor-relief law; (ii) becomes subject to 
an involuntary bankruptcy or insolvency proceeding that is not dismissed within sixty 
(60) Calendar Days; (iii) has a receiver, trustee, liquidator, or custodian appointed for 
it or a substantial portion of its assets, which appointment is not vacated within sixty 
(60) Calendar Days; (iv) makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors; or (v) 
admits in writing its inability to pay debts as they become due; or (f) Eligible 
Customer fails to extend, replace, or otherwise maintain Security in the amount and 
within the time required by Section 7.5, including following a notice of nonrenewal, 
issuer rating reduction, or other event affecting the availability of a Letter of Credit. 
A draw shall not automatically require replenishment to the amount maintained 
immediately before the draw. Following any application of drawn proceeds to an 
amount due, DesertLink shall recalculate the remaining Cumulative Revenue 
Responsibility and the Operational Security then required under this Article. Eligible 
Customer shall replenish only the amount, if any, by which the remaining Operational 
Security is less than the recalculated Required Security Amount, within fifteen (15) 
Business Days after receipt of a Security Notice, or by the applicable in-service date if 
earlier. 
Proceeds drawn solely to prevent the expiration or nonrenewal of a Letter of Credit, 
and cash collateral not yet applied to an identified payment obligation, shall remain 
refundable Security and shall continue to constitute Operational Security until applied 
to an amount then due or released under Section 7.9. Such proceeds and cash collateral 
shall be included in determining the amount of remaining Operational Security and 
shall not create an additional replenishment obligation merely because they are held by 
DesertLink. 
The posting, drawing, holding, replacement, or replenishment of Operational Security 
shall not, by itself, satisfy the secured obligation, reduce Cumulative Revenue 
Responsibility, or produce a TRBAA Credit. Drawn proceeds of Operational Security 
shall become Applied Security Proceeds only when DesertLink applies them to an 
identified Supplemental MTRC, prior-period true-up adjustment, Termination Fee, or 
other secured payment obligation arising under Article 6 or Section 3.3.4. Upon 
application, the proceeds shall reduce that obligation dollar-for-dollar and shall receive 
the TRBAA treatment required by Section 6.8; provided, however, that Applied 
Security Proceeds applied to a Termination Fee shall be administered under Section 
3.3.4 and credited to transmission customer only through the Annual Termination Fee 
Credits provided under Section 6.8. Proceeds of Construction Security applied to Pre-
In-Service Termination Costs or other construction-related obligations shall be treated 
as provided in Sections 3.3.2 and 3.3.3. 
7.7. 
Security Maintenance. Because Required Operational Security is initially one 
hundred percent (100%) of nominal Remaining Cumulative Revenue Responsibility,

36 
 
no separate acceleration concept applies. An incorrect, expired, withdrawn, 
unavailable, or materially misleading Retail Security Certification, or the loss of 
enforceable retail-security rights described in it, is a Material Adverse Credit Event. 
Eligible Customer shall provide replacement direct Security for any resulting 
uncovered amount within fifteen (15) Business Days after receipt of a Security Notice, 
or by the applicable in-service date if earlier. 
7.8. 
Post-Termination Administration and Cash Collateral. DesertLink shall continue 
the annual calculations, invoices, and true-ups required under this Agreement 
following termination of service to, or the departure, permanent cessation, or material 
reduction of service by, the Large Load Customer until the Cumulative Revenue 
Responsibility and all other obligations under this Agreement have been finally 
satisfied, transferred, reassigned, refunded, or otherwise resolved. The Parties intend 
that cash collateral and proceeds of Security be treated as a deposit or deferred liability 
rather than as a Contribution in Aid of Construction, customer financing of 
transmission plant, or a reduction to DesertLink’s rate base. To the extent permitted by 
applicable Commission accounting and ratemaking requirements and tax law, 
DesertLink shall record and administer such amounts as the corresponding annual 
costs and payment obligations arise. The treatment described in this Section is subject 
to the Commission’s Uniform System of Accounts, the Formula Rate, the Protocols, 
applicable Commission orders, and other Applicable Laws and Regulations. If the 
Commission requires a different accounting or ratemaking treatment, DesertLink shall 
implement the required treatment and make corresponding adjustments necessary to 
prevent duplicate recovery and preserve, to the extent permitted, the economic 
allocation established by this Agreement. The Parties shall cooperate in seeking any 
necessary Commission authorization or acceptance.  
Nothing in this Agreement guarantees a particular accounting, ratemaking, or tax 
result. Cash collateral and unapplied Security proceeds shall remain subject to release 
under Section 7.9, including release to reflect an effective prospective reassignment 
under Section 6.9. 
7.9. 
Release of Security. DesertLink shall release excess Operational Security only after 
the applicable Reconciliation Statement becomes final. DesertLink shall release 
Security attributable to an effective prospective reassignment and shall release all 
remaining Security within thirty (30) Calendar Days after final satisfaction of the 
Cumulative Revenue Responsibility and all other secured obligations. Termination 
alone does not require release. 
7.10. Security Does Not Limit Liability. The Required Security Amount is based on 
DesertLink’s then-current estimates and calculations and does not cap, replace, or 
discharge Eligible Customer’s underlying obligations. A shortfall between Security 
and the amount due remains immediately payable to DesertLink. 
7.11. Events of Default; Remedies. Each of the following is an “Event of Default” by 
Eligible Customer: (a) failure to pay any undisputed amount when due that continues 
for ten (10) Business Days after written notice from DesertLink; (b) failure to deliver,

37 
 
maintain, replace, restore, or increase Security when required under this Article 7 or 
Schedule 3 that continues after the applicable cure period; (c) any other material 
breach of this Agreement, including under Section 4.2 or 6.3.6, that continues for 
thirty (30) Calendar Days after written notice from DesertLink or, if the breach cannot 
reasonably be cured within that period, for such longer period, not to exceed ninety 
(90) Calendar Days, as Eligible Customer diligently pursues a cure; and (d) any event 
described in Section 7.6(e). Upon an Event of Default, DesertLink may, subject to 
Applicable Laws and Regulations and the applicable tariffs and agreements: (i) draw 
and apply Security under Section 7.6; (ii) exercise the rights described in Sections 
4.2.6 and 7.2; (iii) before the first Upgrade In-Service Date or Regional Project In-
Service Date, terminate this Agreement under Section 3.3.1; and (iv) pursue any other 
remedy available at law or in equity or before the Commission. No termination after 
an Upgrade In-Service Date or Regional Project In-Service Date releases the 
obligations described in Section 3.3.4.

11. Disputes 
All disputes, claims, or controversies arising out of or relating to this Agreement, including 
any dispute concerning the identification or allocation of Large Load-Driven Upgrades or 
Covered Upgrades; any calculation, update, or recalculation of an Estimated Annual MTRC, 
Final Annual MTRC, Regional Project Allocated ARR, or the MTRC Calculation Template; 
Qualifying Transmission Revenues; Supplemental MTRC; Total Required Revenue 
Commitment; Cumulative Revenue Responsibility; TRBAA Credits; Pre-In-Service 
Termination Costs; the Termination Fee; prospective reassignment; or Security, shall be 
resolved under this Article 11, except that a dispute concerning CAISO’s designation of a 
regional project or assignment of a project cost share shall be resolved under the applicable 
CAISO Tariff procedures. Any payment, refund, credit, or other adjustment resulting from the 
resolution of a dispute under this Article 11 shall be implemented as provided in Section 11.5. 
11.1. Submission and Informal Resolution. In the event of a dispute or claim arising out 
of or relating to this Agreement, the disputing Party shall provide the other Party with 
a written notice describing the dispute (“Notice of Dispute”). The dispute shall be 
referred promptly to designated senior representatives for informal resolution. The 
representatives shall meet or confer within ten (10) Business Days and shall use 
reasonable efforts to resolve the matter within thirty (30) Calendar Days after receipt 
of the Notice of Dispute. This informal process is not a condition to seeking 
emergency relief, filing a FERC complaint, or invoking any ADR processes. 
11.2. Alternative Dispute Resolution. If a dispute is not resolved informally, any Party 
may request Alternative Dispute Resolution (“ADR”). The Parties shall use the ADR 
procedures, neutral-selection process, confidentiality protections, and timing 
requirements specified in the applicable FERC rules. ADR shall be conducted by 
persons knowledgeable in electric utility, transmission, and FERC matters and shall 
not alter a jurisdictional rate, term, or condition unless accepted or approved by the 
FERC. 
11.3. FERC Complaints and Other Rights. Any Party may instead file a complaint, 
petition, or other pleading with the FERC under Section 206 or Section 306 of the 
Federal Power Act, or seek other relief available under the Federal Power Act or 
Applicable Laws and Regulations, and DesertLink may make any filing under Section

40 
 
205 of the Federal Power Act permitted by Section 12.12. No Party’s participation in 
informal negotiations or ADR waives or limits its right to seek FERC action. A final 
ADR determination affecting jurisdictional rates, terms, conditions, charges, or 
Network Upgrades shall be filed with the FERC if required. 
11.4. Costs and Interim Performance. Unless otherwise determined through ADR, the 
Parties shall bear their own costs and share neutral costs as specified by the applicable 
ADR procedure. During a dispute, each Party shall continue performing undisputed 
payment and operational obligations, and shall pay undisputed amounts when due.  
11.5. Implementation of Dispute Determinations; TRBAA. Within thirty (30) Calendar 
Days after a dispute under this Article 11 is finally resolved, whether by written 
agreement of the Parties, a final ADR determination (subject to any required 
Commission filing or acceptance), or a final Commission order (each, a “Dispute 
Determination”), DesertLink shall: (a) update the affected MTRC Calculation 
Template, Schedules, Cumulative Revenue Ledger, Reconciliation Statement, and 
Required Operational Security, as applicable, and serve the updated documents on 
Eligible Customer; and (b) invoice or refund, as applicable, any amount owed between 
the Parties as a result of the Dispute Determination, without interest. To the extent a 
Dispute Determination changes a TRBAA Credit or any other amount previously 
credited to, or recovered from, transmission customers, including any change in 
Supplemental MTRC Receipts or Applied Security Proceeds for a prior Rate Year, 
DesertLink shall record the resulting difference in the TRBA under Section 6.8 and 
flow it through to transmission customers through the TRBAA, and any amount so 
returned by DesertLink to transmission customers shall include interest as provided in 
Section 5.5 of the TO Tariff. If a final Commission order in a proceeding concerning 
DesertLink’s TRBAA requires a change to any TRBAA Credit attributable to this 
Agreement, DesertLink shall implement that order in the TRBA and shall make any 
corresponding updates and adjustments between the Parties under this Section 11.5 as 
if the order were a Dispute Determination. Nothing in this Section reopens the Final 
Annual MTRC or Total Required Revenue Commitment except as required to 
implement a Dispute Determination or as permitted by Section 6.3.1.

Schedule 2 
Qualifying Transmission Revenues Methodology 
1. Purpose and Controlling Principles 
This Schedule establishes the reproducible methodology for calculating projected and actual 
Qualifying Transmission Revenues attributable to the Large Load Facility. It is intended to 
identify wholesale transmission revenues paid by or on behalf of Eligible Customer that are 
attributable to the Large Load Facility and reduce transmission revenues otherwise collected 
from CAISO customers or directly credit DesertLink’s Net Revenue Requirement. Such 
revenues may include applicable TAC revenues and qualifying Wheeling Access Charges or 
other wholesale transmission-access, wheeling, or transmission-service charges under the 
CAISO Tariff or another Commission-accepted arrangement, including charges paid through a 
non-PTO serving entity. The Supplemental MTRC therefore measures only the remaining 
shortfall below the applicable Annual MTRC. 
Qualifying Transmission Revenues shall be counted once in calculating the Supplemental MTRC 
and the Cumulative Revenue Responsibility against the combined Annual MTRC for all Covered 
Upgrades. They shall not also be treated as a TRBAA Credit under Section 6.8 because they 
reduce transmission revenues otherwise collected from CAISO customers. This Schedule does 
not modify CAISO settlement rules, establish a retail rate, impose any obligation on CAISO, or 
alter any cost allocation established under the CAISO Requirements.

4. Applicable Withdrawals 
For each CAISO settlement interval or other reproducible billing interval, Applicable 
Withdrawals shall equal the metered energy withdrawals attributable to the Large Load Facility 
at the metering point identified in Section 2 of this Schedule, expressed in MWh and adjusted as 
follows: 
(a) Imports, exports, station service, auxiliary load, behind-the-meter generation, storage 
charging and discharging, and other injections or withdrawals shall be treated 
consistently with the manner in which they are recognized for the applicable TAC charge 
under the CAISO Tariff. 
(b) Distribution losses and transmission losses shall be included only to the extent they are 
included in the billing determinant for the applicable TAC component. The loss factor or 
method shall be identified in the project-specific table in Section 10 of this Schedule. 
(c) If the Large Load Facility shares a meter or settlement identifier with other load, the 
withdrawals attributable to the Large Load Facility shall be determined from revenue-
quality submeters or another objective allocation method identified in Section 10 of this 
Schedule. An allocation based solely on estimates may be used temporarily but shall be 
reconciled when reliable data become available. 
(d) Withdrawals shall not be counted for a period before the corresponding Annual MTRC is 
included in the Supplemental MTRC calculation under Section 6.4 of the Agreement, 
except where necessary to correct a prior-period error or resettlement. 
5. Applicable TAC Revenue 
Applicable TAC Revenue for an interval shall equal Applicable Withdrawals multiplied by the 
CAISO transmission rate or rates actually applicable to those withdrawals for that interval. The 
calculation shall include only transmission charge components that contribute to recovery of the 
revenue requirement in which DesertLink’s costs are included. It shall exclude retail distribution 
charges, generation charges, non-transmission surcharges, taxes collected for another 
governmental entity, and any other charge that does not contribute to recovery of DesertLink’s 
transmission revenue requirement. 
If CAISO uses a monthly, annual, or other non-interval billing determinant, DesertLink shall 
perform the calculation using that same billing period and determinant. If more than one TAC 
rate or component applies, each component shall be calculated separately before applying the 
DesertLink Allocation Factor. 
6. DesertLink Allocation Factor 
The DesertLink Allocation Factor shall identify the portion of Applicable TAC Revenue 
allocable to DesertLink for the relevant period. Unless a different Commission-accepted method 
is stated in Section 10 of this Schedule, the factor shall be calculated from the same revenue 
requirement, billing determinant, allocation percentage, and other inputs used by CAISO to 
include DesertLink’s net transmission revenue requirement in the applicable TAC rate. 
For each applicable rate component and period:

Schedule 2 - 4 
 
DesertLink Allocation Factor = DesertLink Net Revenue Requirement included in the 
applicable TAC component ÷ Total Net Revenue Requirement recovered through that TAC 
component. 
If DesertLink’s revenue requirement is recovered through a project-specific, zonal, or other 
direct allocation rather than a systemwide factor, the corresponding Commission-accepted 
allocation percentage or rate component shall be used. The supporting workpapers shall identify 
the source and calculation of each factor. 
7. Calculation of Qualifying Transmission Revenues 
Projected and actual Qualifying Transmission Revenues shall be calculated as follows for each 
applicable interval, month, or billing period and then aggregated for the Rate Year or partial Rate 
Year: 
Qualifying Transmission Revenues =  Qualifying TAC Revenue + Qualifying Wheeling and 
Other Wholesale Transmission Revenues ± Applicable Adjustments. 
Qualifying TAC Revenue = Σ [(Applicable Withdrawals × Applicable TAC Rate) × DesertLink 
Allocation Factor]. Qualifying Wheeling and Other Wholesale Transmission Revenues equal 
Wheeling Access Charges and other wholesale transmission-access, wheeling, or transmission-
service charges actually paid by or on behalf of Eligible Customer to CAISO, a Participating TO, 
or a non-PTO transmission or load-serving entity for deliveries serving the Large Load Facility, 
but only to the extent those revenues reduce transmission revenues otherwise collected through 
TAC or directly credit DesertLink’s Net Revenue Requirement. Applicable Adjustments shall 
include only amounts attributable to the Large Load Facility, including CAISO resettlements, 
billing corrections, refunds, charge reversals, balancing-account adjustments, and other 
adjustments that change the qualifying transmission revenue. Bad debt or uncollectible amounts 
shall reduce Qualifying Transmission Revenues only to the extent the corresponding revenue is 
not recovered from another source and is not otherwise included in DesertLink’s Formula Rate 
recovery. 
8. Projections, Actuals, Resettlements, and Customer Changes 
(a) The Annual Projection shall use forecast withdrawals, then-effective or forecast TAC 
rates, the most recent DesertLink Allocation Factor, and known adjustments. The 
workpapers shall separately identify each material assumption. 
(b) The Reconciliation Statement shall replace projected values with actual withdrawals, 
rates, factors, and adjustments for the applicable period. CAISO resettlements or other 
corrections received after a Reconciliation Statement becomes final shall be reflected in 
the next practicable Reconciliation Statement and Annual Update, subject to Section 6.6 
of the Agreement, and any dispute concerning them shall be resolved under Article 11 of 
the Agreement. 
(c) A change in Eligible Customer, Scheduling Coordinator, or retail service provider shall 
not interrupt the calculation or cause the same withdrawals or revenues to be omitted or 
counted more than once. Qualifying Transmission Revenues shall remain associated with 
the Large Load Customer and Large Load Facility, regardless of which Eligible 
Customer is responsible for payment during the applicable period.

(d) If two or more Eligible Customers serve the Large Load Facility during a Rate Year, the 
Qualifying Transmission Revenues and corresponding Supplemental MTRC shall be 
assigned between them based on the periods during which each provided service, unless

Schedule 3 
Credit and Security Standards 
1. Purpose and Application 
This Schedule establishes the forms, delivery, maintenance, replacement, draw, application, and 
release requirements for all Construction Security and Operational Security required under 
Article 7. Except for the limited reduction of direct Operational Security provided in Section 3, 
all Security shall be provided directly by Eligible Customer. 
2. Permitted Forms of Security 
Eligible Customer may provide Security in the form of cash, a Letter of Credit, or any 
combination thereof. DesertLink may accept another form of Security if it determines, in its sole 
discretion, that the form is acceptable. 
Cash collateral shall be delivered in immediately available funds to an account designated by 
DesertLink and shall count dollar-for-dollar toward the applicable Required Security Amount 
while held by DesertLink. 
(a) Construction Security 
Eligible Customer shall provide and maintain all Construction Security directly in one or more 
forms permitted under this Section 2. A Retail Security Certification and Qualifying Retail 
Security Support shall not constitute, reduce, replace, or satisfy Construction Security or any Pre-
In-Service Termination Costs. 
(b) Operational Security 
Except to the extent reduced under Section 3, Eligible Customer shall provide and maintain 
direct Operational Security in one or more forms permitted under this Section 2 in an amount 
equal to one hundred percent (100%) of the nominal Remaining Cumulative Revenue 
Responsibility. 
3. Retail Security Certification 
A current Retail Security Certification reduces the direct Operational Security requirement 
dollar-for-dollar by the amount of Qualifying Retail Security Support identified in that 
certification. It does not reduce Eligible Customer’s underlying obligations, constitute Security 
posted directly with DesertLink, or apply to Construction Security or Pre-In-Service Termination 
Costs. 
Each Retail Security Certification must be substantially in the form of Exhibit A contained in 
Schedule 3 of this Agreement. Eligible Customer shall deliver a Retail Security Certification 
before first relying on Qualifying Retail Security Support to reduce the direct Operational 
Security requirement. The Retail Security Certification shall remain effective unless and until

superseded, withdrawn, or deemed ineffective under this Agreement. Eligible Customer shall 
deliver an updated Retail Security Certification within three (3) Business Days after any 
reduction, draw, expiration, nonrenewal, termination, amendment, loss of enforceable draw or 
application rights, or other event that could impair the certified support. 
With each Reconciliation Statement, DesertLink may identify the amount of Qualifying Retail 
Security Support then reflected in calculating Required Operational Security. That identification 
does not require Eligible Customer to deliver a new Retail Security Certification unless an event 
requiring an update has occurred. 
DesertLink may rely on the certification without reviewing the underlying retail security 
documents in the ordinary course, but may request supporting information after a payment 
default, Credit Review Event, Material Adverse Credit Event, or reasonable basis to question the 
certification. 
4. Letter of Credit Requirements 
If Eligible Customer provides a Letter of Credit as Security, the Letter of Credit must be 
irrevocable, unconditional, transferable, payable at sight, and permit partial and multiple draws. 
It must be issued by a major United States commercial bank or United States branch of a major 
foreign commercial bank rated at least A- by S&P, A3 by Moody’s, or A- by Fitch, in each case 
by at least two of those three agencies, and otherwise be in form and substance reasonably 
acceptable to DesertLink. 
Each Letter of Credit must have an initial stated term of at least twelve (12) months and provide 
DesertLink at least ninety (90) Calendar Days’ prior written notice of nonrenewal. Eligible 
Customer shall provide a conforming extension, replacement Letter of Credit, cash collateral, or 
other Security accepted by DesertLink no later than sixty (60) Calendar Days before the 
applicable expiration date following a notice of nonrenewal, and within fifteen (15) Business 
Days after an issuer rating reduction. 
If Eligible Customer fails to timely provide the required replacement or substitute Security, 
DesertLink may, before the applicable Letter of Credit expires, draw all or any portion of the 
then-available amount and retain the proceeds as cash collateral, apply the proceeds to secured 
obligations, or both. 
5. Security Notices; Maintenance; and Replenishment 
DesertLink may issue a Security Notice whenever it reasonably determines that the Required 
Security Amount exceeds available Security, including as a result of a draw, application of cash 
collateral, change in the Required Security Amount, loss of Qualifying Retail Security Support, 
or other event affecting Security availability. 
Eligible Customer shall provide any required increase, restoration, replacement, or other cure 
within fifteen (15) Business Days after receipt of the Security Notice, or by the applicable in-
service date if earlier. 
6. Draws; Application; and Release

DesertLink may draw against a Letter of Credit, apply cash collateral, or apply another accepted 
form of Security as permitted under Article 7. A draw, the holding of proceeds or cash collateral,

Appendix VI  LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION PROCEDURES

1 
 
 
 
 LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION PROCEDURES (LLIP) 
 
 
Section 1. 
Objectives and Applicability  
1.1 Objectives 
 
The objective of this LLIP is to implement requirements for Large Load interconnections to the 
Participating TO’s Transmission System pursuant to the TO Tariff.  For purposes of this LLIP, 
the “Participating TO” is DesertLink, LLC (“DesertLink”), and the “TO Tariff” is the 
DesertLink, LLC Transmission Owner Tariff.  Because DesertLink is a Non-Load-Serving 
Participating TO and has no End-Use Customers, a Large Load interconnecting under this LLIP 
will not be a retail transmission customer of the Participating TO.   
 
1.2 Applicability  
 
The LLIP is applicable to a Large Load Interconnection Customer that is either (1) proposing to 
interconnect a Large Load to the Participating TO’s Transmission System; (2) seeking to 
increase the capacity of an existing Large Load processed under the LLIP; or (3) with respect to 
an existing load interconnected to the Participating TO’s Transmission System that was not 
processed under the LLIP, seeking an increase of 50 MW or greater.  This LLIP only applies to 
completed Interconnection Requests submitted after the effective date of this Appendix VI to the 
TO Tariff.  Consistent with Section 10A of the TO Tariff, all requests for ECLL Interconnection 
shall be directed to the Participating TO.  An Interconnection Request submitted under this LLIP 
shall constitute the ECLL Interconnection Application, and the Interconnection Studies and the 
Large Load Interconnection Agreement under this LLIP shall constitute the study process and 
the ECLL Interconnection Agreement, respectively, for purposes of Section 10A of the TO 
Tariff.  
 
 
Section 2. 
Definitions

singular of any definition shall include the plural and the plural shall include the singular.  If a 
term with initial capitalization used herein is not defined, such term shall have the meanings 
ascribed to such term in Section 3 of the TO Tariff.

Transmission System that may be affected by the proposed interconnection.   
 
 
Affected System Operator shall mean the entity that owns or operates an Affected System, 
and includes an Affected System Owner as defined in any Cost Recovery Agreement.   
 
 
 
 
Applicable Laws and Regulations shall mean all duly promulgated applicable federal, state 
and local laws, regulations, rules, ordinances, codes, decrees, judgments, directives, or judicial or 
administrative orders, permits and other duly authorized actions of any Governmental Authority.

2

Cost Recovery Agreement shall have the meaning set forth in Section 3 of the TO Tariff.

Flexible Interim Load Interconnection (FILI) Service shall have the meaning set forth in

Large Load Capacity shall mean the maximum capacity of the Large Load at the Point of

Large Load Customer shall mean the End-User that owns, operates, or proposes to develop

Large Load Interconnection Agreement shall mean the interconnection agreement
